committee: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
overview: The Medford City Council Committee of the Whole is a committee comprising all city council members that reviews municipal budgets, proposed ordinances, grant allocations, capital plans, and city policies prior to formal action. The body has been meeting continuously across the recorded archive span from April 13, 2022, to October 13, 2026. Throughout its meetings, the committee conducts detailed departmental hearings, deliberates on legislative amendments, and hears testimony from administration officials, municipal staff, and community stakeholders. It routinely refers refined ordinance drafts, grant packages, and budget priorities to regular council sessions or administrative departments for implementation. At its most recent meeting on October 13, 2026, the committee voted to enter executive session to discuss strategy regarding pending court litigation and adjourned directly from that session.

threads.name: Tree Canopy and Preservation Ordinances
threads.summary: In June 2022, the committee began reviewing a draft tree ordinance to establish public shade tree and private property protections, directing legal counsel to format the draft into existing city code (M06#1, M06#2). After legal drafting stalled in late 2022, the committee referred the matter to subcommittees and requested joint interdepartmental comments (M19#1, M19#3, M19#4). In March 2023, the committee evaluated a zoning-based mitigation model for private trees and discussed creating an advisory Tree Committee (M39#1, M39#2, M39#3). Revisions continued through late 2023 and 2024, culminating in referral of a Tree Committee Ordinance to the full council in July 2025 (M57#1, M81#1, M98#1). The committee approved amendments to the Public Tree Ordinance in July 2026 and referred the paper to the regular meeting (M122#1).

threads.name: Leaf Blower Regulations
threads.summary: The committee began reviewing draft regulations on seasonal leaf blower use and noise limits in May 2022, approving instructions to phase out gas-powered equipment over two years while retaining the paper (M04#1, M04#2). In November 2022, the committee discussed operational enforcement with the Building Commissioner and expanded de minimis exemptions (M23#1, M23#3, M23#5). A comprehensive package of eleven policy amendments was adopted in November 2023 to align operating hours with existing noise rules and eliminate decibel measuring requirements (M59#1). In February 2024, the committee adopted final text amendments on seasonal restrictions and commercial operational plans, voting to report the draft ordinance out of committee as amended (M66#1).

threads.name: Outdoor Dining Ordinance
threads.summary: In December 2022, the committee reviewed a proposal from the Office of Economic Development to establish a permanent outdoor dining ordinance with standardized safety, design, and accessibility guidelines (M28#1, M28#5). The committee refined the draft in February 2023, adding provisions on accessibility enforcement, severability, and tiered fee structures before voting to report the paper out (M35#1). Further revisions were reviewed in March 2023 regarding alcohol licensing, indemnification, safety barriers, and patio heater compliance (M40#1, M40#3, M40#5). The committee officially reported the ordinance out to the City Council favorably as amended in March 2023 (M40#6).

threads.name: Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance Updates
threads.summary: The committee initiated Phase Two zoning ordinance updates in October 2022 to align municipal code with comprehensive city plans for housing, climate, and economic development (M22#1, M22#3). In April 2023, the committee approved a draft Request for Proposals (RFP) specifying vendor criteria, scope of work, and project schedules for a zoning consultant (M41#1, M41#2, M41#4). Following vendor proposal evaluations in December 2023, the committee authorized a selection committee to negotiate a contract with Innes Associates (M62#1). Procurement work continued into September 2026, when the committee approved advancing a new RFP for a consultant to execute the next multi-year phase of the Zoning Updates Project (M124#1).

threads.name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Allocations
threads.summary: In April 2022, the committee reviewed CDBG Year 48 funding recommendations across eleven local service agencies and voted to report the applications out favorably (M01#1, M01#13). The committee reviewed the Year 49 Action Plan proposals in April 2023, placing the matter on file ahead of formal public hearings (M42#1, M42#15). The FY2025 CDBG Action Plan was reviewed and reported out favorably in May 2024 (M74#1, M74#6). Similar annual reviews occurred for FY2026 in April 2025 and for FY2027 in April 2026, with the committee referring the respective plans to regular council sessions for public hearings and final votes (M90#1, M90#3, M110#1, M110#11).

threads.name: Community Preservation Act (CPA) Funding
threads.summary: The committee began evaluating Community Preservation Committee project funding recommendations in January 2023, favorably referring 11 applications for historic preservation, parks, and housing assistance to the regular council meeting (M33#1, M33#12). In February 2024, the committee recommended approval for ten FY24 CPA projects totaling over $1.1 million (M65#1). The FY25 funding round was reviewed in January 2025, resulting in eight project recommendations totaling over $1.8 million being referred to the regular meeting (M85#1, M85#3). In January 2026, the committee favorably referred eleven FY26 projects totaling approximately $2.4 million to the regular City Council meeting (M102#1, M102#13).

threads.name: Annual Municipal Budget Planning and Reviews
threads.summary: The committee establishes annual budget priorities and conducts preliminary departmental reviews prior to executive budget submissions. In May 2022, councilors agreed on five consensus priority recommendations for FY23 before reviewing department proposals (M05#1, M07#1). The committee formalized collective priority lists for FY25 in March 2024, FY26 in March 2025, and FY27 in March 2026 (M68#1, M88#1, M105#1). During each spring cycle, the committee holds extensive preliminary budget hearings with department heads to evaluate personnel, operations, fixed costs, and software modernization plans (M71#2, M91#1, M109#1, M119#1).

threads.name: Food Truck Ordinance Reform
threads.summary: In September 2022, the committee discussed a food truck ordinance draft focused on one-day and special event licenses, referring it to subcommittee (M18#1). The committee reviewed administrative permitting options in February 2023 to streamline event licensing while protecting brick-and-mortar restaurants (M38#1, M38#3). In November 2023, legal counsel advised splitting the proposal into Board of Health operational rules and council land use controls (M58#1, M58#2). The ordinance was kept in committee in March 2024 for redrafting with legal counsel to clarify jurisdictional authority over public ways and city properties (M69#1).
